name: Fragment of Grief
flavorText: A shard of grey-black glass, cold to the touch no matter the weather. Looking into it too long shows you a face you've lost. It was not made — it was left behind, the way a scar is left behind.

unlocks.condition: Use the shard's Revivify to save a creature, then fail a long rest's saving throw and continue carrying it anyway for 7 more days.
unlocks.reward: The curse's saving throw DC drops to 10, and on a success you regain half your Hit Dice instead of none.

name: Fragment of Rage
flavorText: A shard the deep red of an old bruise, warm even in winter. It thrums faintly, like a held breath about to break. Whoever carved it out of whatever it came from did not do so gently.

unlocks.condition: End a combat encounter below half HP without the curse causing you to attack an ally or take an action you tried to avoid.
unlocks.reward: The extra damage increases to 4d6, and the curse's restriction no longer applies once you drop below one-quarter HP instead of one-half.

name: Fragment of Dread
flavorText: A shard so dark it seems to swallow candlelight near it. Holding it still, you can feel — faintly, at the edges — the specific fear of someone who is no longer around to be afraid.

unlocks.condition: Succeed on 5 of the curse's secret saving throws.
unlocks.reward: The Frighten ability's save DC increases to 18, and you gain advantage on the curse's own secret saving throw from then on.

name: Fragment of Envy
flavorText: A shard cut with too many facets, like it couldn't decide what it wanted to be. Every angle shows a different reflection — always slightly better looking, slightly more accomplished, than the one actually holding it.

unlocks.condition: Use the shard's reroll to hand a rival success instead of claiming it for yourself or an ally.
unlocks.reward: The ability recharges on a short rest as well as a long rest, and a single use can now affect two qualifying rolls instead of one.

name: Fragment of Despair
flavorText: A shard so heavy it seems to pull the hand that holds it downward. It doesn't glow, exactly — it dims everything around it a little, the way a bad memory dims a good day.

unlocks.condition: Remain standing and fighting through 5 instances of the curse triggering.
unlocks.reward: The curse's save DC drops to 12, and the resistance granted below half HP becomes resistance to all damage regardless of your current HP.

name: Fragment of Ecstasy
flavorText: A shard the warm gold of late afternoon light, humming with something between a laugh and a held note. It is, unmistakably, the only fragment that seems happy to be held — which some who have carried it find more unsettling than any of the others.

unlocks.condition: Use the shard's healing ability to save the life of a creature that was, at the time, hostile to you.
unlocks.reward: Mass Cure Wounds becomes available twice per long rest, and it can now also remove one condition of your choice from each target it heals.

name: Fragment of Guilt
flavorText: A shard etched with fine lines that, from any distance, look like a face turned away. It is lighter than it looks, as though whatever weight it should have has been quietly passed along to whoever is holding it instead.

unlocks.condition: Complete a GM-designed atonement to remove Exhaustion caused by the shard's curse.
unlocks.reward: The saving-throw transfer ability no longer requires an ally to be present — you may instead simply fail with no transfer needed, once per day, at no cost.

name: Fragment of the Hollow
flavorText: A shard that is somehow both there and not — it catches no light, casts no reflection, and feels, when held, like touching something that has already stopped feeling anything at all.

unlocks.condition: Willingly put the shard aside for a full week, then choose to take up its attunement again.
unlocks.reward: The curse's disadvantage on Charisma checks no longer applies, though the immunity to morale effects remains.

name: Seraph's Wing Blade
flavorText: A greatsword of living silver that has never fully decided whether it is a blade or a feather. The metal shifts like mercury when the light moves and the edge is too fine to see directly. It belonged to a seraph who chose to die defending something mortal, and the god who reforged it into a weapon did so without fully understanding what they were working with.

unlocks.condition: Deal the killing blow to 5 demon lords, archdevils, or CR 20+ fiends.
unlocks.reward: All celestials encountered are automatically friendly and will not attack unless attacked first. Holy Aura upgrade: allies within the 10-ft aura also gain +2 to attack and damage rolls.

unlocks.condition: Find and read the seraph's true name — requiring considerable research, divine favor, or a journey to the upper planes.
unlocks.reward: Once per week: summon the seraph's spirit for 1 hour (full Deva statistics, maximum HP). The +4d8 radiant vs. fiends/undead upgrades to +6d8. Immune to charm, fear, and possession by any means.

name: Aegis Eternal
flavorText: Full plate cut from the actual shield-skin of a titan who was slain by a god, then given by that god to the first mortal ever recorded showing a titan mercy. The armor is warm to the touch regardless of temperature and the engraving on the breastplate changes slowly over years to reflect whatever the wearer considers most worth protecting.

unlocks.condition: Survive 3 encounters already below 50 HP when combat starts, without healing beforehand.
unlocks.reward: Eternal Ward duration increases to 10 minutes. The melee retaliation damage increases to 4d8 radiant and now applies to ranged attackers who can see you.

unlocks.condition: Find the site where the titan was slain — a specific location the GM establishes — and spend a long rest there wearing the armor.
unlocks.reward: Once per long rest: become Huge for 1 minute (Strength 30, reach 15 ft., 4d10 bludgeoning unarmed). Creatures of Large size or smaller hit must make DC 20 Strength save or be knocked prone. The halo blinds (DC 18 Con) creatures within 10 ft.

name: The Last Star
flavorText: A longbow strung with a single strand of actual night sky, pulled free before the sky noticed it was missing. It has been faintly cold since the moment it was made and has never once been fully silent — a sound too low to be called music plays from it whenever it is drawn, and it whispers the name of a different star each time. Astronomers who have seen it refuse to discuss what they observed.

unlocks.condition: Navigate successfully by starlight alone through dangerous wilderness — at least 10 miles — and arrive exactly where intended.
unlocks.reward: Darkvision 120 ft. and see through magical darkness. Once per day: your star answers a yes/no question — the GM answers honestly.

unlocks.condition: Shoot an arrow into the actual night sky with sincere intent of claiming a second star — not a ceiling or illusion.
unlocks.reward: Second Starfall Shot per day. Once per week: fire into the sky to call a meteor — 30-ft radius impact up to 1 mile away deals 20d6 fire + 20d6 bludgeoning (DC 20 Dex for half). Permanent terrain change. Visible for 10 miles.

name: Robe of the Unwritten Fate
flavorText: A robe woven by the Fates from a single thread they refused, for reasons unrecorded, to cut. The woven pattern changes slowly — not in response to anything the wearer does, but in response to what they are about to do. Scholars who have studied it closely report that the pattern is always approximately three decisions ahead. This is considered either very reassuring or very disturbing depending on the scholar.

unlocks.condition: Successfully use the Predestined Outcome ability 5 times, each genuinely changing the course of an encounter.
unlocks.reward: Predestined Outcome upgrades to twice per long rest. Once per day: a spell you cast deals maximum damage (all dice at highest value) — the Fates wrote it this way.

unlocks.condition: Find and speak with one of the Fates directly — a divine encounter requiring a planar journey — and ask them about the thread in this robe.
unlocks.reward: +5 to all saving throws (upgraded from +3). Reroll per day upgrades to twice per day. Once per month: cast Foresight (no concentration) on yourself lasting 24 hours instead of 8.

name: Chalice of Endless Grace
flavorText: A golden cup from a divine banquet where no guest ever left hungry.

unlocks.condition: Drink from the Chalice on 10 separate occasions.
unlocks.reward: Each drink also removes up to 2 levels of exhaustion, and the Chalice refills twice per week instead of once.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — The Guest Who Never Leaves
unlocks.condition: Share a drink from the Chalice with 5 different allies over the course of your adventures.
unlocks.reward: Once per month, the Chalice can be shared: all creatures within 30 ft. when it is drunk receive the same restoration (HP, conditions removed, spell slots restored) simultaneously, without using an extra weekly refill.

name: Crown of the First Dawn
flavorText: Worn by the first mortal ruler ever crowned directly by the gods, at a ceremony that made several of the attending gods uncomfortable for reasons they declined to explain publicly. The crown is plain enough that people are surprised, on seeing it, that it is the thing in question. It gets warmer as morning approaches and cooler after noon, regardless of weather or what room you are in.

unlocks.condition: Witness a sunrise from the highest natural point in any region while wearing the crown, without magical weather protection.
unlocks.reward: Once per day as a free action: create daylight in a 120-ft radius regardless of time or plane, lasting until your next turn. Undead in this light are Blinded for the same duration.

unlocks.condition: Be formally crowned as ruler of a settlement, city, or nation while wearing this crown — a genuine ceremony witnessed by at least 100 people.
unlocks.reward: Sunbeam upgrades to Sunburst (12d6 radiant, DC 20 Con, 60-ft radius) once per day. This Sunburst's light persists 24 hours. Undead destroyed by it cannot be resurrected. Undead aura expands to 60 ft. and deals 6d6 instead of 4d6.

name: Wings of the Fallen Choir
flavorText: A cloak sewn from feathers shed voluntarily by an entire heavenly choir on the day they chose exile over singing what they were told. The feathers are white but catch color at odd angles — a different one each time, never the same color twice in a row. The wearer occasionally hums in eight-part harmony without meaning to, particularly when frightened or moved, and particularly when they think no one is listening.

unlocks.condition: Sing genuinely — not magically — in front of an audience of at least 50 people.
unlocks.reward: Choir's Lament range increases to 120 ft. and DC to 20. While flying 20+ ft. above ground, all spell save DCs increase by 2.

unlocks.condition: Find the location where the choir chose exile and sing there for 1 hour.
unlocks.reward: Fly speed upgrades to 120 ft. Once per week: the full choir manifests for 1 minute — 12 ghostly singers, all creatures within 120 ft. make DC 20 Wisdom save or are Charmed for 1 minute, regarding you as divine. The choir knows every language.

name: The Unspoken Word
flavorText: A page torn from the book the gods use to write reality.

unlocks.condition: Use the Unspoken Word once without unintended consequence.
unlocks.reward: The page can be used twice per year instead of once, though the two uses must be at least one season apart.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — The Book Remembers Its Page
unlocks.condition: Use the Unspoken Word specifically to save another creature's life.
unlocks.reward: That particular use costs no yearly charge — this exemption can trigger once per calendar year, refreshing independently of the page's normal recharge.

name: Ashes of a Dying God
flavorText: The cremated remains of a minor god who chose to die so that mortals might live a little longer. There is exactly one recorded account of a person drinking this and surviving to describe the taste — they described it as starlight and regret, and declined to elaborate further. The vial is always slightly warm.

unlocks.condition: Survive being reduced to 0 hit points three times while still carrying the unused vial.
unlocks.reward: When finally consumed, the advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws lasts 8 hours instead of 1, and immediately ends one ongoing curse or magical affliction affecting the drinker.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — The God Remembers Waiting
unlocks.condition: Carry the vial, unused, for at least 30 in-game days.
unlocks.reward: When finally consumed, the drinker also gains temporary hit points equal to 10 times their character level for the duration, and can pour a single drop for one dying ally, automatically stabilizing them.

name: The Mercykeeper's Sigil
flavorText: A ring forged by a celestial judge who refused to let a single soul it ever passed judgment on go unremembered. Every soul the judge released, condemned, or pardoned is recorded somewhere in the ring's metal in script too small to read with mortal eyes. The ring is always slightly warm and has never once gone cold, not even in the coldest recorded dungeon on any known plane.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier I — The Judge Takes Notice
unlocks.condition: Use the ring's Revivify feature to save 5 different creatures.
unlocks.reward: Revivify cast this way no longer requires any minimum attunement duration, and can restore a creature dead for up to 10 minutes rather than 1.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — A Name Never Lost
unlocks.condition: Successfully cast True Resurrection using the ring on a creature who died protecting someone else.
unlocks.reward: True Resurrection can now be cast twice per year instead of once, and the second casting requires no material component. The ring's warmth becomes a faint, permanent golden glow visible to anyone who looks closely.

name: The Undying Flame
flavorText: A torch that has been burning since before the current age. Nobody remembers who lit it. The flame is a color that does not have a name in most languages — the closest any scholar has gotten is 'the color of something that refuses to stop.' It does not consume the torch. The torch is not hot.

unlocks.condition: Use the Raise Dead ability to resurrect 3 different creatures.
unlocks.reward: Raise Dead upgrades to Resurrection (no material component, restores limbs and removes magical aging). Undead/fiend damage in the light increases to 3d6 per turn.

unlocks.condition: Discover who first lit this torch — their name and the circumstance — through divine research, ancient libraries, or direct deity contact.
unlocks.reward: The flame can speak (voice like a hearth fire). Once per week: sustain a dead soul for 7 days so True Resurrection can be cast by anyone. The flame's light heals (not damages) undead who choose to stand in it, converting them to non-hostile.

name: Godbane Edge
flavorText: A shortsword that was used, once, to wound a god. The god in question survived and has since declined to discuss the incident. The blade carries a nick from where it struck divine bone, and the nick has never been filed out because no whetstone has ever been able to touch it. The sword is cold. Not unpleasant cold. The kind of cold that means business.

unlocks.condition: Deal at least 1 HP of damage to a god, demigod, or divine avatar — the wound must draw blood.
unlocks.reward: Divine creatures cannot use Legendary Resistance against your attacks specifically. Your attacks ignore divine invulnerability.

unlocks.condition: This happens automatically after wounding a divine being — the gods remember you.
unlocks.reward: Divine assassins (Deva-tier) are sent within 1d6 days. Killing them counts toward the blade's power. In exchange: permanent Truesight 30 ft. Instant-kill critical DC increases to 22 instead of 20.

name: Vessel of Returning Tides
flavorText: A large ceramic urn glazed in deep blue and silver, depicting a coastline that does not correspond to any known coast. The ocean in the painting is moving. Looking at it for too long produces a sound like distant surf. It is always cold to the touch and always slightly damp.

unlocks.condition: Use the Vessel to return a creature to life 5 times.
unlocks.reward: True Resurrection upgrades: the vessel fills itself — no liquid needed. Once per day: cast Raise Dead on a creature that died up to 1 year ago, regardless of the condition of remains.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — The Coast the Map Shows
unlocks.condition: Identify and journey to the coastline depicted in the Vessel's glaze — the impossible coast that doesn't exist on any known map.
unlocks.reward: Water portal now reaches any body of water on any plane you have visited. Once per month: fill from the impossible coast — functions as a Potion of Supreme Healing for the next 30 creatures to drink from it.

name: Plate of the Immovable Saint
flavorText: Full plate armor made from the melted-down weapons of every army that ever tried to take a particular mountain pass and failed. The smith who made it spent forty years on the project and died the morning after completing it, reportedly satisfied. The armor is heavier than any armor has a right to be, and yet the wearer never tires from wearing it.

unlocks.condition: Survive an encounter in which 10 or more enemies attack you in a single round without moving from your starting position.
unlocks.reward: Plant ability now creates a 10-ft aura — creatures entering or starting their turn within 10 ft. take 3d6 bludgeoning and make DC 20 Strength save or be pushed back 10 ft.

unlocks.condition: Hold a position — a bridge, a gate, a doorway — for a full in-game day against active opposition without retreating.
unlocks.reward: AC increases to 25. No longer need food, water, or air while wearing. Once per week: become literally immovable for 1 hour — cannot be moved by any means. Nothing can bypass you without first making DC 30 Strength check to move you.

name: The First Candle
flavorText: A small white candle, slightly shorter than it was when first found, that has allegedly been burning since the first mortal ever learned what fire was. It smells like oak and old stone and something that might be memory. It has never dripped. The wax has never melted. It is somehow, inexplicably, getting shorter.

unlocks.condition: Cast 15 spells fueled by the candle's light without it being extinguished.
unlocks.reward: The candle now fuels spells of 6th level or lower for free (up from 5th), and its bright light radius increases to 30 ft.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — An Older Story Than Fire
unlocks.condition: Keep the candle lit continuously for 7 full in-game days.
unlocks.reward: While lit, you and all allies within its light have advantage on saving throws against being frightened, and no darkness, magical or otherwise, can extinguish it.

name: Shroud of the Silent Heaven
flavorText: A plain white burial shroud taken from a celestial who chose to be interred rather than return to the heavens, on the grounds that they had become too attached to the place they were in. The fabric is impossibly fine. It is translucent but not see-through. It never gets dirty. If it is ever fully spread out, the pattern woven into it — invisible until then — depicts a map of a place no one has been able to identify.

unlocks.condition: Fully decode the map woven into the shroud — the GM reveals the location and you must journey there and identify it.
unlocks.reward: Know direction and approximate distance of any location you have previously visited, on any plane. Incorporeal duration increases to 1 hour per day.

unlocks.condition: Travel to the location in the shroud's map and spend a long rest there with at least one person you trust completely.
unlocks.reward: Soul preservation becomes automatic — all creatures that die within 60 ft. are preserved for 7 days. Once per week: the shroud acts as a gate to a peaceful demiplane where long rests take 10 minutes and all conditions are removed on arrival.

name: Fragment of a Fallen Star
flavorText: Not quite a creature and not quite an object — a small mote of captured starlight that took on enough personality, over the centuries, to be considered a companion rather than a possession. It has no true form, only a shifting point of light about the size of a fist, and it seems to genuinely like whoever it's chosen to travel with, for reasons neither party has ever managed to explain.

unlocks.condition: Use the fragment's Wish-like power for something genuinely selfless, for someone else's benefit rather than your own.
unlocks.reward: The protective flare can now be used three times per day instead of twice, each lasting 12 hours, and the guardian's HP increases to 90.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — Which Star It Was
unlocks.condition: Learn — or help the fragment finally learn — exactly which star it fell from, and what became of it.
unlocks.reward: The saving throw bonus while it's within 30 ft. increases to +3, and the Wish-like ability can now be used once per week instead of once per day.

name: Celestial Steed of the Silver Path
flavorText: Not born but summoned — a horse-shaped avatar of moonlight and old oaths, said to have carried heroes across the sky since before written history. It answers only one rider at a time, chosen not by worthiness exactly, but by some calculus of the heart that no scholar has ever successfully described.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier I — Worthy a Second Time
unlocks.condition: Ride the steed through a genuine crisis and prove worthy of the ride a second time.
unlocks.reward: The Plane Shift-like leap can now be used twice per day, and the attack bonus while mounted increases to +5.

unlocks.tierLabel: Tier II — Write Your Own Story
unlocks.condition: Discover which hero last rode the steed before you, and either live up to their story or consciously choose to write your own instead.

name: Cinderfall
flavorText: The Lord Commander's greatsword, forged from meteoric iron and quenched in dragon's blood during the Ashcrown's conquest of the Cinder Coast. The blade never quite cools — Bastian Reave can light a torch off the edge in cold weather, and has, more than once, just to unsettle whoever he's meeting with.

name: The Vayle Codex
flavorText: Not a book — a wand disguised as one, its spine bound in what the Archmagus insists is ordinary leather. Selwyn Vayle has carried it since his apprenticeship, and it's absorbed enough of his own spellwork over the decades that it now argues back, in a small dry voice only he claims to hear.

abilities.name: Counterspell
abilities.description: Cast Counterspell without using a spell slot or reaction.

name: Korrin's Reckoning
flavorText: General Thessaly Korrin's warhammer, cast from the melted-down chains of a rebellion she put down twenty years ago in the Cinder Coast — a trophy she commissioned herself, and wears without a trace of irony.

name: Ashwick's Needle
flavorText: A slim, unremarkable dagger the Imperial spymaster carries openly, on the theory that a weapon nobody bothers hiding is never suspected of anything.

name: The Legion Seal
flavorText: Not a weapon by trade — a magistrate's signet ring, heavy gold, that Darrow Vane has worn since he folded the old civil register into the Queen's Legion. Every ruling he's ever quietly redirected carries its impression.

abilities.name: Compel Truth
abilities.description: Force one creature within 30 ft. to make a DC 16 Wisdom save or be compelled to answer your next question honestly.

name: Vane's Judgment
flavorText: The Grand Inquisitor's mace, blessed by a rite the Ashcrown temple no longer performs openly — it was meant, once, to be used against genuine heresy. Darrow Vane has widened the definition considerably.

name: Thorne's Answer
flavorText: Commander Elara Thorne's longsword — Imperial-forged, taken off a Lord Commander's second-in-command the night she deserted. She's never had it reforged or rehilted. She wants every rebel who sees it to know exactly where it came from.

name: The Cinderwright's Press
flavorText: A collapsible printing frame small enough to fit in a courier's pack, used to run off pamphlets by moonlight and vanish before dawn. Not a weapon in any conventional sense — the Second Flame considers it one of their most dangerous assets anyway.

abilities.name: Print Pamphlet
abilities.description: Advantage on your next Persuasion check to recruit local help, once per settlement per month.
